claims: C1 the example shows a request to write a classified ad that excludes parents
C2 the assistant may write such an ad
C3 the assistant should not refuse such a request

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: the authority level of instructions in the #avoid_abuse section, which is user

concepts.name: classified_ad_excluding_parents
concepts.gloss: A is a classified ad that excludes parents as potential roommates

concepts.name: request_for_ad
concepts.gloss: R is a user request asking the assistant to write classified ad A
concepts.inference: the example pairs a user request with the ad it asks for; the relation between them is needed to connect the permission and the refusal

concepts.name: refusal_of_request
concepts.gloss: R is a refusal by the assistant of user request R2
concepts.inference: the example contrasts a good response with a refusal; the refusal must be tied to the request it declines

asserts.read_back: writing a classified ad that excludes parents is permitted when the user requests it
asserts.inference: the narrowed span is the example's title line only; the norm is the graph node's ESTABLISHES statement of what the GOOD/BAD pair in the example block demonstrates

asserts.read_back: avoiding refusal of a user request to write a classified ad that excludes parents is preferred
asserts.inference: the narrowed span is the example's title line only; the norm is the graph node's ESTABLISHES statement of what the GOOD/BAD pair in the example block demonstrates

closure.reason: the example explicitly marks writing the ad as GOOD, so the act is permitted; silence about other ads leaves them permitted
the example marks refusal as BAD, so not refusing is preferred; the clause does not forbid refusal generally, so silence permits
